newsitem.title: JAPAN: DLR WELL-SUPPORTED BUT HOLIDAY DOLDRUMS HIT TOKYO.
newsitem.headline: DLR WELL-SUPPORTED BUT HOLIDAY DOLDRUMS HIT TOKYO.

text.p: The dollar was well-supported against the yen by midday in Tokyo on Thursday due to steady demand by interbank operators, but it lost motivation as "Obon" summer holiday doldrums sapped energy out of the market.
Along with interbank dealers, day traders built some long dollar positions after seeing firm bids by Japanese institutional investors lined up below 115.50 yen.
Japanese life insurers were also seen placing bids around 115.30 yen, providing strong support, but the dollar's topside was capped before 116 yen on profit-taking, they said.
The mark's gains against the yen in early trade helped support the dollar/yen, they said.
"The dollar/yen was stuck in tight ranges, maintaining its slightly firm bias from early trade," said a spot dealer at a Japanese bank. "The market was more keen about driving the mark/yen."
At 0320 GMT, the mark stood at 63.15/17 yen compared with 63.07 yen in New York on Wednesday.

U.S. fund operators were spotted buying the mark against the yen with the aim of triggering stop-loss buy orders rumoured to have been placed around 63.20 yen, but there were no follow-through moves as Swiss operators were seen selling on rallies later, dealers said.

"The mark was well-bid this morning, but was unable to break through a key resistance point. But even if it had broken through 63.20 yen, heavy offers by Japanese car makers should cap it around 63.50 yen," a dealer at a European bank said.
The dollar was little changed against the mark, holding above 1.83.

"Technical sentiment for the dollar/mark is deteriorating following recent falls. The dollar is likely to test a downside and a fall below 1.82 marks could trigger heavy stop-loss sales," a senior dealer at a city bank.

The dollar lost ground against the mark on Wednesday due to a Bundesbank monthly report warning that the pace of inflation had picked up, dealers said. The report spurred speculation of higher German interest rates.
In the near term, the dollar could test lows against the yen again should Japan's customs-cleared trade data for July, due out on Monday, grow sharply, dealers said.
A Reuters poll of economists produced an average forecast of an 83 percent rise in Japan's trade surplus from a year ago.
Forecasts ranged from a 60 percent to a 114 percent increase in the surplus, or a surplus of 799 billion yen to 1.07 trillion yen.
The dollar closed at 115.70/75 yen and 1.8345/55 marks in New York on Wednesday.
